title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

This guide consolidates Redwood Inference's people operations standards for hiring, onboarding, performance cycles, feedback, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers. Follow the procedures below to ensure consistent candidate experience, predictable hiring timelines, and fair, documented performance practices.

Contents
1. Hiring process overview
2. Interviewing and scorecards
3. Offer, compensation, and approvals
4. Onboarding: Day 0-90 plan
5. Performance and feedback cycles
6. Manager guide: responsibilities and checklists
7. Templates and examples
8. Related systems and owners

## 1. Hiring process overview
Purpose: Standardize how we run openings, evaluate candidates, and make offers while minimizing time-to-hire and ensuring diverse, high-quality hires.

Key roles and ownership
- Hiring manager: defines role, scorecard, and final interview loop; owner of technical evaluation.
- Recruiter (people-ops/talent): sources candidates, schedules interviews, and manages offer pipeline.
- Interview panel: 3-5 interviewers covering skills, culture fit, and role-specific competencies.
- Hiring committee (for IC level >= L5 and managers): reviews final decisions for calibration.

Target SLAs (service-level agreements)
- Requisition posted -> first candidate screened: 7 business days
- Interview loop completed after first onsite/loop: target 10 business days
- Offer decision after final interview: 3 business days
- Time-to-offer (requisition open -> offer accepted): target median 30 calendar days

Diversity & Inclusive hiring
- All public roles must include at least two diverse slates or active outreach strategies.
- Use structured scorecards and standardized questions to reduce bias.

Process checklist (high level)
1. Hiring manager creates/reviews job requisition and role scorecard. (Owner: HM)
2. Recruiter posts to Greenhouse and target job boards; begins sourcing. (Owner: Recruiter)
3. Screen phone/initial interview with recruiter: role fit and compensation expectations. (Owner: Recruiter)
4. Technical/functional interview loop scheduled with standardized scorecards. (Owner: HM + Interviewers)
5. Final interviews + hiring manager debrief + calibration if required. (Owner: HM)
6. Offer approval, compensation band check, and approving signatures. (Owner: People Ops + Finance as needed)
7. Offer extended, candidate accepts, and start date agreed. (Owner: Recruiter/People Ops)

## 2. Interviewing and scorecards
Structured interviewing principle: Ask the same core questions for every candidate for a given role and capture numeric scores and short notes.

Scorecard fields (required for every loop):
- Core competencies (0-4): role-specific technical skills
- Problem solving (0-4): ability to approach unknowns
- Collaboration & communication (0-4)
- Role passion / craft fit (0-4)
- Culture & company values (0-4)
- Recommendation (Hire / No Hire / Hire with reservations)

Rubric guidance (example)
- 4 = Exceptional: exceeds role expectations; multiple concrete impact examples
- 3 = Strong: meets expectations and would be a good contributor
- 2 = Borderline: some gaps; would need development
- 1 = Weak: lacks key skills and evidence
- 0 = No evidence / absent

Interview best practices
- Begin every interview with a 2-minute intro and 1-minute candidate questions.
- Use STAR framework for behavioral prompts.
- Timebox: 45-60 minutes per interview.
- Document at least 2-3 concrete examples in notes for any score >=3 or <=1.

Conflict-of-interest & recusal
- If an interviewer has a close personal relationship with the candidate, they must recuse from the hiring decision and disclose to the recruiter.

## 3. Offer, compensation, and approvals
Compensation bands
| Level | Base salary band (US, USD) | Typical equity % (for ICs) | Approval required |
|-------|-----------------------------|---------------------------|------------------|
| L1-L2 | 90,000 - 140,000            | 0.01% - 0.03%             | Hiring manager     |
| L3    | 140,000 - 190,000           | 0.03% - 0.07%             | Recruiter + People Ops |
| L4    | 190,000 - 260,000           | 0.07% - 0.20%             | People Ops + Finance  |
| L5+   | 260,000+                    | 0.20%+                    | People Ops + Finance + Exec approval |

Approval workflow
1. Hiring manager drafts compensation proposal (base + bonus + equity + sign-on if applicable).
2. Recruiter / People Ops verifies band and documents rationale in Greenhouse offer packet.
3. If above band or special terms, route to Finance for sign-off (72-hour turnaround target).
4. Exec approval for L5+ or strategic hires (5 business days target).

Offer template checklist
- Offer letter PDF (templated in Workday/HRIS)
- Compensation breakdown: base, bonus, equity, benefits summary
- Start date and first-week plan summary
- Contingencies: background check, proof of employment eligibility
- Relocation/remote equipment if applicable

## 4. Onboarding: Day 0-90 plan
Objective: Get new hires to meaningful contribution while integrating them into our culture and processes.

Pre-start (Owner: Recruiter + IT + Hiring manager)
- New hire packet sent with first-week agenda, responsibilities, and required forms (Workday, tax forms).
- IT equipment order confirmed and shipped (target 7 business days before start).
- Slack + email account provisioned; teams added; access to key docs granted.

Day 0-7 (Orientation & setup)
- Day 0: Welcome + company overview (People Ops).
- IT/Access checklist completed: laptop, VPN, KMS access, Google/Email, GitHub, internal confluence.
- Manager 1:1 set for every workday first week.
- Mandatory trainings assigned: security, data handling, acceptable use (complete by day 7).

Week 2-4 (Role ramp)
- Initial 30-day goals set by manager with clear success metrics.
- Paired sessions with two teammates; product & architecture walkthroughs scheduled.
- First feedback touchpoint at day 30 (manager + people-ops).

Month 2 (Ownership & feedback)
- Candidate takes on first scoped project with measurable deliverable.
- Manager provides biweekly feedback; people-ops checks in on culture fit and workload.

Month 3 (Checkpoint)
- 90-day review: evaluate against initial 30/60/90 goals; document in HRIS and share written feedback.
- Decide on continued ramp, promotion eligibility, or support actions.

Onboarding checklist (table)
| Item | Owner | Target completion |
|------|-------|-------------------|
| Accounts provisioned | IT | Day 0 |
| Security training | New hire | Day 7 |
| 30-day goals set | Manager | Day 14 |
| First project assigned | Manager | Day 30 |
| 90-day review completed | Manager + People Ops | Day 90 |

## 5. Performance and feedback cycles
Cadence
- Continuous feedback: encouraged between peers and manager year-round.
- Quarterly check-ins: informal alignment on goals and blockers.
- Mid-year calibration & annual review: formal documented assessment and calibration across teams.

Performance rating framework (summary)
- Exceeds Expectations (E)
- Meets Expectations (M)
- Needs Improvement (N)

Calibration & fairness
- People Ops runs cross-functional calibration sessions each mid-year and end-of-year. Hiring managers must submit written evidence and 3-5 examples per rating.
- Calibration anchors: business impact, ownership, complexity of work, and scope of role.

Performance improvement (process for Needs Improvement)
1. Manager documents performance gaps with examples and notifies people-ops.
2. Create a 60-90 day Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with clear milestones and owner responsibilities.
3. Weekly 1:1 tracking and mid-point review.
4. Final assessment determines continuation, extended support, or termination (People Ops advised and legal reviewed as needed).

Feedback best practices
- Use frequent, timely examples; focus on behavior and impact, not intent.
- Encourage peer feedback via Slack 'shoutouts' and quarterly 360s for cross-functional roles.

Compensation and promotion cycles
- Promotions: Nomination by manager with documented impact and calibration review. Typical timeline 8-12 weeks for review and compensation adjustments.
- Merit increases: aligned to annual performance cycle; off-cycle increases possible for market corrections (People Ops + Finance approval).

## 6. Manager guide: responsibilities and checklists
Manager responsibilities (ongoing)
- Hire: define scorecard, interview, and make informed hiring decisions.
- Onboard: deliver 30/60/90 plan and regular feedback.
- Develop: run career conversations, identify stretch projects, and support growth.
- Evaluate: gather evidence for performance reviews and participate in calibration.

Manager 30/60/90 checklist
- Day 0-30: Introduce team, set first deliverable, schedule recurring 1:1s.
- Day 31-60: Assign ownership of a project, identify development goals, and provide feedback weekly.
- Day 61-90: Run 90-day review, set medium-term objectives (quarterly).

Hiring manager interview preparation (quick checklist)
- Confirm scorecard and core interview questions before scheduling.
- Share interview agenda and role context with panel.
- Brief interviewers on bias mitigation and rubric scoring.

Manager escalation & people-ops support matrix
- Low urgency (coaching, workload): Manager -> People Ops Slack channel (response within 2 business days).
- Medium urgency (performance concerns, conflict): Manager -> People Ops partner + HR case opened (response within 24 business hours).
- High urgency (legal, safety, termination): Immediate People Ops + Legal escalation (phone and case opened within 4 hours).

## 7. Templates and examples
Candidate scorecard (copy into Greenhouse):
- Candidate name: __________
- Role: __________
- Interviewer: __________
- Scores: Core competencies (0-4), Problem solving (0-4), Collaboration (0-4), Recommendation (Hire/No Hire)
- Notes: 2-3 examples supporting score

Sample 30-day goals template (manager writes):
- Goal 1 (impact metric): e.g., Complete integration tests for feature X with <=5 regressions
- Goal 2 (learning): e.g., Finish architecture walkthroughs for subsystem Y
- Goal 3 (collaboration): e.g., Lead two cross-team troubleshooting sessions

PIP template headlines:
- Date issued | Performance gaps | Specific measurable goals | Review cadence | Consequences if goals not met

## 8. Related systems and owners
- Applicant tracking system: Greenhouse (Owner: People Ops / Recruiting)
- HRIS / payroll: Workday (Owner: People Ops + Finance)
- Learning & training: Docebo / LinkedIn Learning (Owner: People Ops)
- Security & access: IT provisioning runbooks (Owner: Eng Infra)
